edges.reason: Seven/eight/nine products can be built independently by equal groups; the earlier two-through-six fact table is useful preparation but not a logical requirement to learn those products.
The target explicitly distinguishes boundary length from area. Perimeter meaning is required for that contrast, not all rectangle/square perimeter computations.
Two-digit columns support larger numerical areas. Repeated unit-square counts or decomposed multiplication can also compute an area, so no fixed dimension range is imposed by this preparation link.
edges.scope: computing areas with two-digit side lengths

edges.reason: The tiled-region interpretation explains what length times width counts. The Geometric Measurement Progression develops that interpretation before treating multiplication as a formula; knowing the formula alone does not certify the tiling procedure.
edges.scope: Understanding rectangle and square area formulas as counts of square units

edges.reason: The rectangle/square area formulas count equal square units, so the meaning of area and its uniform unit are part of the asserted result.
edges.scope: interpreting length times width as unit-square count
